claims.text: EF Core docs: calling LINQ operators just builds an in-memory representation of the query; the query is only sent to the database when results are consumed (a for/foreach loop, or ToList/ToArray/Single/Count and their async overloads).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/querying/how-query-works.md, "When queries are executed"

claims.text: EF Core docs: the database provider identifies which parts of a LINQ query can be evaluated in the database and translates them to database-specific query language (SQL); a query is sent once and the result set returned.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/querying/how-query-works.md, "The life of a query"

claims.text: EF Core docs: by default (single query mode, used in the absence of any configuration), EF loads related entities by introducing JOINs into the same single query, not a separate query per included navigation.

EfOrderRepository's FindAsync and ListByCustomerAsync are each one expression-bodied statement chaining Where/Include/OrderBy onto db.Orders, ending in FirstOrDefaultAsync/ToListAsync; neither method body uses async/await.

Live run against the stage-1 lab: GET /api/v1/orders for two different signed-in seeded customers (anh.tran@example.com, chau.nguyen@example.com) returns two disjoint order lists, each containing only that customer's own orders.
